input_text: Kim is sued by Jim for medical malpractice. To prove that Kim was a bad doctor, Jim introduces evidence that Kim told her friend that she cheated on all her medical school exams.

extraction.input_text: Kim is sued by Jim for medical malpractice. To prove that Kim was a bad doctor, Jim introduces evidence that Kim told her friend that she cheated on all her medical school exams.

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The statement was made out of court, as Kim told her friend about cheating on her exams.
arguments.evidence_span: Kim told her friend that she cheated on all her medical school exams.

arguments.text: The statement contains a clear assertion, specifically an admission of cheating on medical school exams.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires a statement that contains an assertion.
arguments.evidence_span: she cheated on all her medical school exams

arguments.text: The statement is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted, namely that Kim cheated on her exams to demonstrate she was a bad doctor.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: To prove that Kim was a bad doctor, Jim introduces evidence that Kim told her friend that she cheated on all her medical school exams.

arguments.text: The statement qualifies as a party-opponent admission under FRE 801(d)(2) because it is offered against Kim by the opposing party Jim in the malpractice suit.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(d)(2)(A) excludes a party-opponent's own statement offered against them from the definition of hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: Kim is sued by Jim for medical malpractice. To prove that Kim was a bad doctor, Jim introduces evidence that Kim told her friend that she cheated on all her medical school exams.
